title: Narrative tenses
note: BUILT 2026-09-05 (b2/auto), from the 2026-08-29 empty stub. Weaves the four past tenses: past simple is the spine, past continuous the background, past perfect and its continuous everything earlier. C29 timeline on card 0 against the tenses already taught (a2_past_simple, a2_past_continuous, b1_past_continuous_2, b1_past_perfect, b2_past_perfect). B12 Check is a sort of English sentences into the three jobs (bins named by job per B17, sort_cz false per B20, taught form bolded per C37) — Czech cannot pick the tense. A14: every past-perfect item carries a stated past anchor (when we got there / by the time / it was her first flight), and no item's distractor list offers a reading that is also correct (G4). B3/B6/B4 authored quiz_options on every item, same lemma, carrying the errors a Czech learner makes. B11 lemma cue on every gap. E7 Use is error-correction, one error per sentence (E2), never a correct sentence (E9).

items.en: The storm **started** at four.
items.cz: Bouřka začala ve čtyři.
items.explanation: It moves the story on → past simple.
items.explanation_cz: Posouvá příběh dál → past simple.

items.en: First he knocked, then he **rang** the bell.
items.cz: Nejdřív zaklepal, pak zazvonil.
items.explanation: It moves the story on → past simple.
items.explanation_cz: Posouvá příběh dál → past simple.

items.en: The lights went out and the room **fell** silent.
items.cz: Zhasla světla a v místnosti nastalo ticho.
items.explanation: It moves the story on → past simple.
items.explanation_cz: Posouvá příběh dál → past simple.

items.en: We **were waiting** outside when the storm started.
items.cz: Čekali jsme venku, když začala bouřka.
items.explanation: It was already running → past continuous.
items.explanation_cz: Už probíhalo → past continuous.

items.en: While she **was writing** the report, the power failed.
items.cz: Zatímco psala zprávu, vypadl proud.
items.explanation: It was already running → past continuous.
items.explanation_cz: Už probíhalo → past continuous.

items.en: The dog **was barking** when I opened the gate.
items.cz: Pes štěkal, když jsem otevřel bránu.
items.explanation: It was already running → past continuous.
items.explanation_cz: Už probíhalo → past continuous.

items.en: When we got to the stop, the bus **had already left**.
items.cz: Když jsme došli na zastávku, autobus už odjel.
items.explanation: It was finished before the story reached it → past perfect.
items.explanation_cz: Skončilo dřív, než tam příběh došel → past perfect.

items.en: She couldn't pay because she **had left** her wallet at home.
items.cz: Nemohla zaplatit, protože si nechala peněženku doma.
items.explanation: It was finished before the story reached it → past perfect.
items.explanation_cz: Skončilo dřív, než tam příběh došel → past perfect.

items.en: The room was empty; everyone **had gone** home.
items.cz: Místnost byla prázdná; všichni už šli domů.
items.explanation: It was finished before the story reached it → past perfect.
items.explanation_cz: Skončilo dřív, než tam příběh došel → past perfect.

items.en: We were waiting outside when the storm started.
items.cz: Čekali jsme venku, když začala bouřka.
items.gap: We ____ outside when the storm started. (wait)
accepts: We were waiting outside when the storm started.
items.wrong: We were wait outside when the storm started.
items.explanation: The waiting was already running when the storm landed on it → **were waiting**.
items.explanation_cz: Čekání už probíhalo, když přišla bouřka → **were waiting**.

items.en: She was checking her email while the meeting went on.
items.cz: Kontrolovala si e-maily, zatímco schůze pokračovala.
items.gap: She ____ her email while the meeting went on. (check)
accepts: She was checking her email while the meeting went on.
items.wrong: She was check her email while the meeting went on.
items.explanation: Two long actions at once → **was checking**. she takes **was**.
items.explanation_cz: Dvě dlouhé akce zároveň → **was checking**. she má **was**.

items.en: The dog was barking when I opened the gate.
items.cz: Pes štěkal, když jsem otevřel bránu.
items.gap: The dog ____ when I opened the gate. (bark)
accepts: The dog was barking when I opened the gate.
items.wrong: The dog was bark when I opened the gate.
items.explanation: The barking was the background; opening the gate is the short event → **was barking**.
items.explanation_cz: Štěkání je pozadí, otevření brány krátká událost → **was barking**.

items.en: They were painting the hall when we arrived.
items.cz: Zrovna malovali chodbu, když jsme přijeli.
items.gap: They ____ the hall when we arrived. (paint)
accepts: They were painting the hall when we arrived.
items.wrong: They was painting the hall when we arrived.
items.explanation: they takes **were**: the painting was under way when we arrived.
items.explanation_cz: they má **were**: malování probíhalo, když jsme přijeli.

items.en: I wasn't listening when he explained the rules.
items.cz: Neposlouchal jsem, když vysvětloval pravidla.
items.gap: I ____ when he explained the rules. (not / listen)
accepts: I wasn't listening when he explained the rules.
I was not listening when he explained the rules.
items.wrong: I didn't listening when he explained the rules.
items.explanation: Negative background: **wasn't** + listening, not didn't + -ing.
items.explanation_cz: Záporné pozadí: **wasn't** + listening, ne didn't + -ing.

items.en: While she was writing the report, the power failed.
items.cz: Zatímco psala zprávu, vypadl proud.
items.gap: While she ____ the report, the power failed. (write)
accepts: While she was writing the report, the power failed.
items.wrong: While she was wrote the report, the power failed.
items.explanation: **while** introduces the long action → **was writing**; the failure cuts it.
items.explanation_cz: **while** uvádí dlouhou akci → **was writing**; výpadek ji přeruší.

items.en: Where were you sitting when the film started?
items.cz: Kde jsi seděl, když začal film?
items.gap: Where ____ when the film started? (you / sit)
accepts: Where were you sitting when the film started?
items.wrong: Where you were sitting when the film started?
items.explanation: Question order: **were** + you + sitting. No **did** with a continuous form.
items.explanation_cz: Pořádek v otázce: **were** + you + sitting. S průběhovým tvarem se **did** nepoužívá.

items.en: When we got to the stop, the bus had already left.
items.cz: Když jsme došli na zastávku, autobus už odjel.
items.gap: When we got to the stop, the bus ____. (already / leave)
accepts: When we got to the stop, the bus had already left.
items.wrong: When we got to the stop, the bus had already leave.
items.explanation: Getting to the stop is the anchor; the leaving is earlier → **had already left**.
items.explanation_cz: Příchod na zastávku je kotva, odjezd je dřív → **had already left**.

items.en: By the time the doctor arrived, the pain had stopped.
items.cz: Než přijel doktor, bolest už přestala.
items.gap: By the time the doctor arrived, the pain ____. (stop)
accepts: By the time the doctor arrived, the pain had stopped.
items.wrong: By the time the doctor arrived, the pain had stop.
items.explanation: **by the time** + past simple gives the point; the pain stopped before it → **had stopped**.
items.explanation_cz: **by the time** + minulý čas dává bod; bolest přestala dřív → **had stopped**.

items.en: She couldn't pay because she had left her wallet at home.
items.cz: Nemohla zaplatit, protože si nechala peněženku doma.
items.gap: She couldn't pay because she ____ her wallet at home. (leave)
accepts: She couldn't pay because she had left her wallet at home.
She could not pay because she had left her wallet at home.
She could not pay because she'd left her wallet at home.
She couldn't pay because she'd left her wallet at home.
items.wrong: She couldn't pay because she had leaved her wallet at home.
items.explanation: The wallet was left before she tried to pay → **had left**. leave is irregular: left.
items.explanation_cz: Peněženku nechala doma dřív, než chtěla platit → **had left**. leave je nepravidelné: left.

items.en: The room was empty; everyone had gone home.
items.cz: Místnost byla prázdná; všichni už šli domů.
items.gap: The room was empty; everyone ____ home. (go)
accepts: The room was empty; everyone had gone home.
items.wrong: The room was empty; everyone had went home.
items.explanation: The empty room is the moment; the leaving came earlier → **had gone**, not had went.
items.explanation_cz: Prázdná místnost je ten okamžik, odchod byl dřív → **had gone**, ne had went.

items.en: I recognised the street because I had been there before.
items.cz: Poznal jsem tu ulici, protože jsem tam už byl.
items.gap: I recognised the street because I ____ there before. (be)
accepts: I recognised the street because I had been there before.
I recognised the street because I'd been there before.
items.wrong: I recognised the street because I had be there before.
items.explanation: Recognising is the moment in the story; the earlier visit takes **had been**.
items.explanation_cz: Poznání je okamžik v příběhu, dřívější návštěva má **had been**.

items.en: It was her first flight; she had never been on a plane.
items.cz: Byl to její první let; nikdy předtím neletěla letadlem.
items.gap: It was her first flight; she ____ on a plane. (never / be)
accepts: It was her first flight; she had never been on a plane.
It was her first flight; she'd never been on a plane.
items.wrong: It was her first flight; she had never be on a plane.
items.explanation: The first flight is the past frame; everything before it takes **had never been**.
items.explanation_cz: První let je minulý rámec, všechno před ním má **had never been**.

items.en: When I checked my bag, I saw someone had taken my laptop.
items.cz: Když jsem zkontroloval tašku, viděl jsem, že mi někdo vzal notebook.
items.gap: When I checked my bag, I saw someone ____ my laptop. (take)
accepts: When I checked my bag, I saw someone had taken my laptop.
items.wrong: When I checked my bag, I saw someone had took my laptop.
items.explanation: Checking the bag is the anchor; the theft was earlier → **had taken**, not had took.
items.explanation_cz: Kontrola tašky je kotva, krádež byla dřív → **had taken**, ne had took.

items.en: They had locked the gate by the time the last guest arrived.
items.cz: Než dorazil poslední host, už bránu zamkli.
items.gap: They ____ the gate by the time the last guest arrived. (lock)
accepts: They had locked the gate by the time the last guest arrived.
They'd locked the gate by the time the last guest arrived.
items.wrong: They had lock the gate by the time the last guest arrived.
items.explanation: The guest's arrival is the point; the locking is earlier → **had locked**.
items.explanation_cz: Příchod hosta je ten bod, zamykání je dřív → **had locked**.

items.en: He failed the test because he had not revised.
items.cz: Neudělal test, protože se neučil.
items.gap: He failed the test because he ____. (not / revise)
accepts: He failed the test because he had not revised.
He failed the test because he hadn't revised.
items.wrong: He failed the test because he had not revise.
items.explanation: Negative earlier past: **had not** + revised. The failing is the later point.
items.explanation_cz: Záporná dřívější minulost: **had not** + revised. Neúspěch je pozdější bod.

items.en: We had been waiting for an hour when the train finally came.
items.cz: Čekali jsme už hodinu, když vlak konečně přijel.
items.gap: We ____ for an hour when the train finally came. (wait)
accepts: We had been waiting for an hour when the train finally came.
We'd been waiting for an hour when the train finally came.
items.wrong: We had been wait for an hour when the train finally came.
items.explanation: How long up to that moment → **had been waiting**, not the passive had been waited.
items.explanation_cz: Jak dlouho až do toho okamžiku → **had been waiting**, ne trpné had been waited.

items.en: His eyes were red; he had been crying.
items.cz: Měl červené oči; plakal.
items.gap: His eyes were red; he ____. (cry)
accepts: His eyes were red; he had been crying.
His eyes were red; he'd been crying.
items.wrong: His eyes were red; he had been cry.
items.explanation: The red eyes are the evidence left by the crying → **had been crying**.
items.explanation_cz: Červené oči jsou stopa po pláči → **had been crying**.

items.en: The pitch was wet because it had been raining all night.
items.cz: Hřiště bylo mokré, protože celou noc pršelo.
items.gap: The pitch was wet because it ____ all night. (rain)
accepts: The pitch was wet because it had been raining all night.
The pitch was wet because it'd been raining all night.
items.wrong: The pitch was wet because it had been rain all night.
items.explanation: All night of rain explains the wet pitch → **had been raining**.
items.explanation_cz: Celá noc deště vysvětluje mokré hřiště → **had been raining**.

items.en: She was exhausted; she had been driving since dawn.
items.cz: Byla vyčerpaná; řídila už od svítání.
items.gap: She was exhausted; she ____ since dawn. (drive)
accepts: She was exhausted; she had been driving since dawn.
She was exhausted; she'd been driving since dawn.
items.wrong: She was exhausted; she had been drive since dawn.
items.explanation: **since dawn** measures the time up to that moment → **had been driving**.
items.explanation_cz: **since dawn** měří dobu až do toho okamžiku → **had been driving**.

items.en: They had been living in Brno for years before they moved.
items.cz: Bydleli v Brně roky, než se odstěhovali.
items.gap: They ____ in Brno for years before they moved. (live)
accepts: They had been living in Brno for years before they moved.
They'd been living in Brno for years before they moved.
items.wrong: They had been live in Brno for years before they moved.
items.explanation: Years of living, up to the move → **had been living**.
items.explanation_cz: Roky bydlení až do stěhování → **had been living**.

items.en: How long had you been working there before you left?
items.cz: Jak dlouho jsi tam pracoval, než jsi odešel?
items.gap: How long ____ there before you left? (you / work)
accepts: How long had you been working there before you left?
items.wrong: How long you had been working there before you left?
items.explanation: Question order: **had** + you + been working. Leaving is the point you measure to.
items.explanation_cz: Pořádek v otázce: **had** + you + been working. Odchod je bod, ke kterému měříš.

items.en: We arrived at six, ate quickly and caught the last bus.
items.cz: Přijeli jsme v šest, rychle se najedli a stihli poslední autobus.
items.gap: We arrived at six, ate quickly and ____ the last bus. (catch)
accepts: We arrived at six, ate quickly and caught the last bus.
items.wrong: We arrived at six, ate quickly and had caught the last bus.
items.explanation: Three events in order — all past simple. Nothing here is earlier than the story.
items.explanation_cz: Tři události za sebou — všechny past simple. Nic tu není dřív než příběh.

items.en: First he knocked, then he rang the bell.
items.cz: Nejdřív zaklepal, pak zazvonil.
items.gap: First he knocked, then he ____ the bell. (ring)
accepts: First he knocked, then he rang the bell.
items.wrong: First he knocked, then he had rung the bell.
items.explanation: **first … then** already puts them in order, so past simple does the whole job.
items.explanation_cz: **first … then** je už seřadilo, past simple stačí.

items.en: The train pulled in and everyone stood up.
items.cz: Vlak zastavil a všichni vstali.
items.gap: The train pulled in and everyone ____. (stand up)
accepts: The train pulled in and everyone stood up.
items.wrong: The train pulled in and everyone had stood up.
items.explanation: Two events, one after the other → past simple **stood up**.
items.explanation_cz: Dvě události po sobě → past simple **stood up**.

items.en: He finished the letter and posted it the same day.
items.cz: Dopis dopsal a ještě týž den ho poslal.
items.gap: He finished the letter and ____ it the same day. (post)
accepts: He finished the letter and posted it the same day.
items.wrong: He finished the letter and had posted it the same day.
items.explanation: The same day, in order → past simple **posted**. No earlier layer here.
items.explanation_cz: Týž den, po sobě → past simple **posted**. Žádná dřívější vrstva.

items.en: The lights went out and the room fell silent.
items.cz: Zhasla světla a v místnosti nastalo ticho.
items.gap: The lights went out and the room ____ silent. (fall)
accepts: The lights went out and the room fell silent.
items.wrong: The lights went out and the room had fallen silent.
items.explanation: One event follows the other → past simple **fell**, the irregular form of fall.
items.explanation_cz: Jedna událost následuje druhou → past simple **fell**, nepravidelný tvar od fall.

items.en: While I was packing, I realised I had lost the tickets.
items.cz: Zatímco jsem balil, zjistil jsem, že jsem ztratil lístky.
items.gap: While I was packing, I realised I ____ the tickets. (lose)
accepts: While I was packing, I realised I had lost the tickets.
While I was packing, I realised I'd lost the tickets.
items.wrong: While I was packing, I realised I had lose the tickets.
items.explanation: Three layers: packing is the background, realising is the event, losing is earlier → **had lost**.
items.explanation_cz: Tři vrstvy: balení pozadí, zjištění událost, ztráta dřív → **had lost**.

items.en: The kitchen smelled of smoke; someone had burnt the toast.
items.cz: V kuchyni byl cítit kouř; někdo spálil toast.
items.gap: The kitchen smelled of smoke; someone ____ the toast. (burn)
accepts: The kitchen smelled of smoke; someone had burnt the toast.
The kitchen smelled of smoke; someone had burned the toast.
items.wrong: The kitchen smelled of smoke; someone had burn the toast.
items.explanation: The smell is the moment; the burning came before it → **had burnt**.
items.explanation_cz: Zápach je ten okamžik, spálení bylo dřív → **had burnt**.

items.en: He was still typing when the deadline passed.
items.cz: Pořád ještě psal, když uplynula lhůta.
items.gap: He ____ when the deadline passed. (still / type)
accepts: He was still typing when the deadline passed.
items.wrong: He was still type when the deadline passed.
items.explanation: **still** + the background form: the typing was under way when the deadline passed.
items.explanation_cz: **still** + průběhový tvar: psaní probíhalo, když lhůta uplynula.

items.en: By the time she called, I had already fallen asleep.
items.cz: Než zavolala, už jsem usnul.
items.gap: By the time she called, I ____ asleep. (already / fall)
accepts: By the time she called, I had already fallen asleep.
By the time she called, I'd already fallen asleep.
items.wrong: By the time she called, I had already fall asleep.
items.explanation: Her call is the point; falling asleep happened before it → **had already fallen**.
items.explanation_cz: Její hovor je ten bod, usnutí bylo dřív → **had already fallen**.

points: A story needs more than one past tense. Each one has its own job.
The **events** move the story forward — past simple.
The **background** was already running — past continuous.
Anything from **before** the story — past perfect.

cards.title: The events, in order

rows: First he knocked, then he **rang** the bell.
We arrived at six, ate quickly and **caught** the last bus.
The lights went out and the room **fell** silent.

points: Past simple is the spine. Everything else hangs off it.
Two things that simply happened in order are both past simple.
Do not reach for **had** just because the sentence is about the past.

cards.title: The background

rows: We **were waiting** outside when the storm started.
While she **was writing** the report, the power failed.
They **were arguing** quietly while the children slept.

points: The continuous is already running when the event lands on it.
**when** usually introduces the short one, **while** the long one.

cards.title: Before the story

rows: When we got to the stop, the bus **had** already left.
We **had been** waiting for an hour when the train finally came.
the point it is earlier than
When we got to the stop…

points: Past perfect always needs a point in the story to be earlier **than**.
With no such point, past simple is the honest tense.

cards.title: Which one?

rows: Did it move the story on?
Was it finished before that moment?
How long had it run up to that moment?

points: Read the whole sentence. The other clause tells you which job this one has.
Czech marks the order with *už*, *zrovna*, *zatímco* — English marks it with the tense.

cards.title: Common mistakes

rows: ~~I was cook when the phone rang.~~
I **was cooking** when the phone rang.
~~We arrived at six and had caught the last bus.~~
We arrived at six, ate quickly and **caught** the last bus.
~~How long you had been working there?~~
How long **had you** been working there before you left?

points: Past perfect is not a politer past simple. It needs something to be earlier than.
**was** and **were** take -ing. **had** takes a past participle.
